newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: PDVSA CARDON REFORMER BACK ON THU/FRI - OFFICIAL.
newsitem.headline: PDVSA CARDON REFORMER BACK ON THU/FRI - OFFICIAL.

text.p: Venezuela's state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) said its 45,000 bpd reformer in the Cardon refinery was in tests and was expected to return to full capacity by Thursday or Friday, a spoeswoman said on Monday.
The plant was hurt by a fire in a related hydro- desulphurisation unit on July 28 and forced PDVSA to declare force majeure on all six of the refinery's gasoline shipments in August.
Traders said that two of the 230,000-barrel cargoes were cancelled while four customers accepted alternative supplies.
The refinery produces both anti-dumping and reformulated gasoline, mostly for the U.S. market.
Three more small gasoline shipments were also affected by the force majeure after the Curacao refinery also suffered a major fire on July 31.

A Curacao refinery official said he expected throughput to reach 170,000 bpd, versus a normal 185,000 bpd, between August 22 and August 25. He expected the average loss of processing throughout the month of August to be 65,000 bpd.
Both refineries are major exporters of gasoline and other refined products to the U.S. and Caribbean markets, but no other products were affected by the force majeure.
